home.lead: Open Hearth supports Christian families with a grant for each newborn child. The money, the queue, and the draw are visible to everyone. This is a reference charter and website: the ledger is a worked example, and donations are not accepted.
home.scaleLead: The amount depends only on the child's order of birth inside this registered marriage.
home.step1Text: Both spouses have belonged to one Christian church for at least a year. The marriage is registered by the state.
home.step2Text: Marriage and birth certificates are not published. The endorsement and the family code are.
home.step3Text: The application is visible to everyone. An objection that names a rule pauses the payout until it is reviewed.
home.step4Text: If the money covers every approved application, payouts follow the approval date. If it does not, there is a public draw.
home.promise1Text: The balance equals income minus expenses and payouts. The finances page checks that identity.
home.promise2Text: Hardship and a large family change the weight and the quota. They do not let anyone reorder the queue in private.
home.promise3Text: The order is built from a published seed and HMAC. The button on the round page repeats the calculation.
home.promise4Text: The child-record hash is unique. A second application for the same child is rejected in public.

apply.title: How to apply
apply.lead: Applications open after the fund is registered. Below is the procedure the site will carry out, and a calculator for the public card.
apply.s1Text: The child was born in this marriage, is under one year old on the application day, the marriage is registered, and church membership is at least a year.
apply.s2Text: State marriage and birth certificates. The public ledger receives the birth month, the marriage year, and a family code, not document numbers.
apply.s3Text: The pastor of your church confirms membership and checks the documents. Hardship needs a second pastor from another church.
apply.s4Text: For fourteen days the application sits on the open list. An objection has to name a specific rule.
apply.s5Text: After the window the application receives an approval date. From that day, the child's age no longer removes the family's right: waiting for money is not punished.
apply.s6Text: The scale amount is sent by transfer or stablecoin. The fund pays the fee and shows it as an expense. The family receives the full amount.
apply.hardship: Hardship confirmed by a second pastor
apply.notEligible: Less than a year of membership — the application will not be approved.
apply.weightNote: The figures are thousandths of weight. Waiting after approval and the regional factor are not included: they depend on the round date and the whole queue.
apply.publicCard: Published: child {order}, membership {years} years, hardship — {hardship}. No name and no address.

queue.title: Queue and draw
queue.lead: Approved applications wait for money. If on the round date their sum exceeds the distributable balance, the hearth-quota-1 draw begins.

finances.title: Open finances
finances.lead: Every line of the sample ledger is visible. There are no salaries in this period; the category exists and is zero.
finances.hashNote: In the sample ledger the hash is SHA-256 of the public string demo-receipt. In operation the hash is taken from the receipt file, and the reviewer keeps the file.
finances.giveTitle: How the fund will receive support
finances.giveLead: After registration: a bank transfer, a monthly card, and the legal entity's crypto addresses. The addresses below are deliberately unusable.
finances.rails: A bitcoin or ether gift is booked in dollars on the day it arrives. Later price movement is a separate line, so it does not change the amount promised to a family. A stablecoin is preferred. The treasury is a 2-of-3 multisig.

rules.title: Fund rules
rules.lead: These rules change only by a newly published version. A current round is not replayed under later rules.
rules.a1Text: The fund receives donations and pays a Christian family a sum for a newborn child. It does not replace a church and does not test belief beyond the pastor's endorsement.
rules.a2Text: The child was born in one state-registered marriage. The family has belonged to a Christian church for at least a year. On the application day the child is under one year old. The pastor of that church must endorse the family.
rules.a3Text: The first child in this marriage is 5,000 dollars, the second 6,500, the third 7,000, and the fourth and each later child 7,500. Order is counted inside this marriage, not across earlier marriages.
rules.a4Text: Family code, church and city, pastor with an initial, birth month, birth order, years of membership, amount, status, date, and a hardship mark without a diagnosis.
rules.a5Text: Full names, street address, document numbers, medical records, and contact details. The child-record hash is stored apart, and the site cannot read it.
rules.a6Text: If approved applications do not exceed the distributable balance, payouts follow the approval date. The operating reserve is at least 5,000 dollars and at least ten percent of the balance.
rules.a7Text: Nine tenths of the distributable balance are offered to the draw, and one tenth stays for the next month. Twenty percent of the pool is a priority lane for a fourth or later child, or for confirmed hardship. Unused priority budget rolls into the open lane.
rules.a8Text: The base is 1. Add 0.15 for each full year of membership after the first, up to 0.75. Add 0.25 for a third child or 0.50 from the fourth. Add 0.35 for hardship. Add 0.05 for each full month of waiting after approval, up to 0.30. If a country has been underpaid relative to its share of the queue, the weight is multiplied by 1.2.
rules.a9Text: One church receives at most two payouts in a round. There is no manual jump of the queue. A board member's family cannot receive a payout during service or for a year after it.
rules.a10Text: The pastor checks the certificates, the date the family joined the church, and that the child is of this marriage. For fourteen days anyone may name the rule that was broken. A diagnosis is neither required nor published.
rules.a11Text: Hosting, accounting, fees, legal work, review, and salaries if any are published before payment. An expense above the board threshold needs two approvals. A family's grant is not reduced by a fee.
rules.a12Text: Money is collected only after registration. Practical options are an Armenian foundation, an Estonian nonprofit association, or a US 501(c)(3) if American donors need a deduction. The treasury is in dollars, and the reporting is public in any of these forms.

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: Why not always pay in queue order?
faq.a1: Queue order is used when the money covers everyone. The draw starts only when it does not. Otherwise the latest applicants would wait without an end.
faq.a2: There is no quiet skip. Hardship confirmed by two pastors adds weight and a place in the priority quota. Selection inside the quota is still random and published.
faq.a3: Three public categories: housing, income, and medical. The details stay with the pastors and the reviewer. The ledger shows only the category.
faq.q4: What if the child grows while the family waits?
faq.a4: Age is checked on the application day. Waiting for a round does not cancel a right that was already recognized.
faq.a5: The marriage must be valid under the civil law of the country. A rite with no civil effect is not enough. Where a church marriage is the civil marriage, it is accepted.
faq.a6: The scale is in dollars so families in different countries see the same promise. A gift's exchange rate is fixed on the day it arrives.
faq.a7: A family without a year of membership, without a registered marriage, without an endorsement, with a child older than one year on the application day, or with a repeated record of the same child.
faq.a8: Not in this version. The grant is tied to a birth in the marriage. An extension requires a new public version of the rules, not a board exception for one family.

pastors.title: How to endorse a family
pastors.lead: A pastor does not set the amount and does not move the queue. The pastor attests to facts the fund cannot see.
pastors.d1Text: The church is Christian, it has existed for more than a year, and the pastor is named in public. A new church is published separately before its first endorsements.
pastors.d2Text: Check the state certificate. The year of marriage is published. The number is not.
pastors.d3Text: Check the birth certificate: the date is under one year on the application day, the child is of this marriage, and the order is among the children of this marriage.
pastors.d4Text: Both spouses have been on the church roll for at least a year. The pastor states the full number of years.
pastors.d5Text: Only together with a pastor of another church. The published category is housing, income, or medical. A medical history is not uploaded to the site.
pastors.d6Text: The endorsement appears in the ledger under the pastor's code. A false attestation is a public reason to suspend the pastor and review that pastor's applications.
pastors.statement: I, {pastor}, pastor of {church}, attest: family {family} has belonged to the church for {years} full years; the child in this marriage is number {order}; {hardship}. The marriage and birth certificates were checked. Full names and the address are not sent to the ledger.
pastors.hardshipYes: hardship is confirmed by a second pastor
pastors.preview: This is what everyone will see
pastors.formNote: The form sends nothing. After registration the signature will be tied to the pastor's account.
pastors.flagLead: If a pastor has four or more endorsements and more than half of them claim hardship, the row is marked. That is not an accusation. It is a reason for a public question.
